newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE ends review, prepares for Lisbon summit.
newsitem.headline: OSCE ends review, prepares for Lisbon summit.

text.p: Europe's security organisation, racked by internal dispute at its last summit, has grown in stature, notching up a notable success in supervising Bosnia's post-war elections, the body's top official said on Friday.

But Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, chairman-in-office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said the group had to remain flexible and adapt to changes as Europe entered the 21st century.
"Three years ago...we got the impression...that interest in the OSCE had declined," Cotti told the OSCE's decision-making permanent council, based in Vienna.
"Today, no such doubts are to be heard. The OSCE is once again an important partner in international dialogue," he said.
Cotti was addressing the council at the end of a three-week review conference held in preparation of the OSCE's biannual summit in Lisbon on December 2 and 3.
The last OSCE summit, held in Budapest two years ago, was marred by rows over the war raging in Bosnia and warnings from Russia that the whole continent faced renewed confrontation.

But the organisation, the only European body of which both the United States and Russia are members, is widely considered to have developed into more than a forum for debate, winning praise for its work in overseeing elections, human rights, arms control and security.

Once again, issues relating to Russia and Bosnia were likely to dominate the Lisbon summit to be attended by leaders from the OSCE's 54 member states, including U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Envoys at the review conference agreed to extend the OSCE's mission to Bosnia until the end of 1997, and then to consider a further extension into 1998.
But debate in Lisbon will also focus on whether the OSCE should carry out the same supervisory role of municipal polls in Bosnia as it had during nationwide elections in September.
"Our view is that the OSCE mandate concerning municipal elections should be the same as this year," Cotti said.
Bosnian municipal elections were due to be held at the same time as the national polls but were postponed until next year due to registration irregularities.

The more complex question of a future security structure for Europe will figure high on the summit agenda, with Russia, in particular, pushing for the OSCE to be given the authority to wield more influence over Europen security.

Moscow, suspicious of NATO's planned eastward expansion, is pressing for a firm commitment in Lisbon to set up a group of powerful members within the OSCE to guide Europe with more legal authority as a counterbalance to NATO.
But Cotti, whose country hands over the OSCE chairmanship to Denmark at the end of the year, said there was unlikely to be any firm decision taken in Lisbon.

The Swiss minister said the summit also had to address changes to the OSCE's widely-respected election monitoring body and to the structure of the current 10 long-term missions in such countries as Tajikistan, Macedonia and Moldova.

Following Albania's disputed general election this year, OSCE observers issued a critical report over irregularities. But Tirana dismissed the criticism, referring instead to milder comments from other observers, such as the Council of Europe.
Cotti said the OSCE and the Council, which also oversees human rights and elections, should in future decide which body should take responsibility to monitor a given election.

The OSCE roadshow moves to Lisbon next week where a preparatory meeting will pore over reports compiled during the Vienna review conference and draw up draft documents for leaders to consider at the summit.
